subject: American Bison
fact: American bison are the largest land mammals in North America.

subject: Moose
fact: Moose are the largest members of the deer family.

subject: Elk
fact: Male elk grow large antlers that are shed and regrown each year.

subject: White-Tailed Deer
fact: White-tailed deer raise their white tails like flags when alarmed.

subject: Mule Deer
fact: Mule deer have especially large ears that resemble a mule's ears.

subject: Caribou
fact: Both male and female caribou can grow antlers.

subject: Pronghorn
fact: Pronghorns are among the fastest land animals in North America.

subject: Bighorn Sheep
fact: Bighorn sheep have special hooves that help them grip steep rocky slopes.

subject: Mountain Goat
fact: Mountain goats are strong climbers with rough hoof pads for rocky terrain.

subject: Musk Ox
fact: Musk oxen have extremely warm underfur called qiviut.

subject: Grizzly Bear
fact: Grizzly bears have powerful shoulder muscles that help them dig.

subject: American Black Bear
fact: American black bears can be black, brown, cinnamon, or even nearly white.

subject: Polar Bear
fact: Polar bears have black skin beneath their thick fur.

subject: Gray Wolf
fact: Gray wolves live and hunt in family groups called packs.

subject: Coyote
fact: Coyotes communicate with howls, yips, and barks.

subject: Red Fox
fact: Red foxes use large ears to pinpoint small animals hidden under grass or snow.

subject: Arctic Fox
fact: Arctic foxes have fur-covered foot pads that help insulate them from cold ground.

subject: Bobcat
fact: Bobcats are named for their short bobbed tails.

subject: Canada Lynx
fact: Canada lynx have large furry paws that act like snowshoes.

subject: Cougar
fact: Cougars can leap great distances and climb trees easily.

subject: Wolverine
fact: Wolverines have strong jaws and broad paws for traveling over snow.

subject: American Badger
fact: American badgers have powerful forelimbs and long claws for digging.

subject: Striped Skunk
fact: Striped skunks can spray a strong-smelling liquid when threatened.

subject: North American River Otter
fact: River otters are playful swimmers with webbed feet and streamlined bodies.

subject: Sea Otter
fact: Sea otters use rocks as tools to open hard-shelled food.

subject: American Beaver
fact: Beavers build dams that can create ponds and wetlands.

subject: North American Porcupine
fact: Porcupines are covered with thousands of sharp quills made from modified hairs.

subject: Raccoon
fact: Raccoons have very sensitive front paws that help them explore objects and food.

subject: Virginia Opossum
fact: Virginia opossums are North America's only native marsupials north of Mexico.

subject: Nine-Banded Armadillo
fact: Nine-banded armadillos can jump straight upward when startled.

subject: Eastern Cottontail
fact: Cottontail rabbits are named for the fluffy white underside of their tails.

subject: Snowshoe Hare
fact: Snowshoe hares have large furry feet that help them move over snow.

subject: Black-Tailed Prairie Dog
fact: Prairie dogs live in large burrow systems sometimes called towns.

subject: American Pika
fact: Pikas collect grasses and flowers into hay piles for winter food.

subject: Eastern Gray Squirrel
fact: Gray squirrels bury nuts and sometimes forget them, helping new trees grow.

subject: American Red Squirrel
fact: Red squirrels often store cones in piles called middens.

subject: Groundhog
fact: Groundhogs are large squirrels that dig deep burrows.

subject: American Marten
fact: American martens are agile forest mammals that climb trees well.

subject: Fisher
fact: Fishers are forest-dwelling relatives of weasels and are excellent climbers.

subject: Ringtail
fact: Ringtails have long striped tails and are nimble climbers of rocky cliffs and trees.

subject: Bald Eagle
fact: Bald eagles build some of the largest bird nests in North America.

subject: Golden Eagle
fact: Golden eagles use powerful talons to catch prey.

subject: Great Horned Owl
fact: Great horned owls have feather tufts that look like ears.

subject: Snowy Owl
fact: Snowy owls have thick feathers that cover even their legs and feet.

subject: Wild Turkey
fact: Wild turkeys can fly short distances despite spending much of their time on the ground.

subject: Sandhill Crane
fact: Sandhill cranes perform energetic dancing displays with jumps and bows.

subject: Whooping Crane
fact: Whooping cranes are among the tallest birds in North America.

subject: American Flamingo
fact: American flamingos get their pink color from pigments in the food they eat.

subject: Brown Pelican
fact: Brown pelicans often plunge-dive from the air to catch fish.

subject: Atlantic Puffin
fact: Puffins use their wings to swim underwater.

subject: Common Loon
fact: Loons are excellent divers with legs set far back on their bodies.

subject: Greater Roadrunner
fact: Greater roadrunners can run quickly and often hunt lizards, insects, and small snakes.

subject: American Alligator
fact: Alligators use powerful tails to swim through water.

subject: Gila Monster
fact: Gila monsters are venomous lizards with bead-like scales.

subject: Desert Tortoise
fact: Desert tortoises spend much of their lives in underground burrows.

subject: Common Snapping Turtle
fact: Snapping turtles have strong jaws and long tails.

subject: Bullfrog
fact: American bullfrogs are large frogs with deep booming calls.

subject: Hellbender
fact: Hellbenders are giant salamanders that live in cool fast-moving streams.

subject: Monarch Butterfly
fact: Monarch butterflies can migrate thousands of miles between North America and Mexico.

subject: American Lobster
fact: American lobsters have large claws and live on the rocky seafloor of the North Atlantic.
